label: text
text: To-morrow is the anniversary of St. Matthew.

label: text
text: As from to-day the P. & O. Ranking Corporation office will be at Prince's Building, Chater Road (premises formerly occupied by the Yokohama Specie Bank).

label: text
text: Moon-cake. feast " falls tomorrow. " The "China Mattle" article on the festival appears on page 6. The Chinese Maritime Customs will be closed for the day.

label: text
text: The French Government requested Mr. Chen Lu, Chinese Minister at Paris, to inquire whether the Chinese Government would take any interest in the Betheloe Institute in Paris. After careful consideration, by the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Education, it has now been decided that an annual sum of Francs 15,000 be subscribed by the Chinese Government, which amount will immediately be remitted to the above mentioned institute.

label: text
text: The quality of "samples" must necessarily indicate that of the goods in stock if the advertiser is permanently to benefit from his enterprise. The ment and well finished shoe horns which have been received by many residents will doubtless lead many to test the qualities of the well known "K" make of shoes to advertise, which the shoe horns were sent out by Mackintosh and Co., Ltd., men's wear specialists.

label: text
text: Montreal, September 3.—Sir Henry Thornton, President of the Canadian National Railways, giving his opinion on the Grand Trunk Pacific settlement, declared that apart from its legal aspects, the situation was opposed to the best interests of the Dominion. Moreover, even broader Imperial considerations might be involved. I feel that not only the Railway but the Empire has been well served by an amicable settlement being reached.

label: text
text: Sydney, August 5th The movement for the secession of Western Australia from the Federation which has been in the air for several years has now been launched definitely by the formation, at a large public meeting at Perth, of an organisation provisionally entitled "the Secession League," officials have been appointed and fighting fund has been opened. The position is probably not serious, but it is interesting in view of a similar movement, in Tasmania.

label: text
text: The Government have appropriated £25,000 for publicity in connection with the British Industries Fair in London and Birmingham from February 21 to March 4 next.

label: text
text: Peking, September 12.—The Peking Wireless Station at Tientan, which recently established its business office in front of the Chienmen Gate, commenced handling private telegrams to-day.

label: text
text: Winnipeg, August 5.—The Earl of Clarendon, visiting the British families settled in Manitoba under the Empire settlement scheme reports that at the 10 points inspected the finds everybody doing well and giving every promise of success.

label: text
text: Nairobi, August 5. — The Glasgow steamer "Clain Mackenzie" (6,544 tons) has discharged at the new deep-water pier at Killindini, on the south side of the island on which Mombasa stands. This is the first occasion in the history of Kenya that a vessel has discharged her cargo alongside the shore. The ship was given a great welcome by the population of Mombasa.

label: text
text: Miss Agnes Millar, of "Glasgow, was fined £7 18s. 6d... at Dundalk for trying to import into Ireland a man's suit without paying duty. She pleaded that she did not read newspapers and knew nothing about Customs regulations. She was taking the suit to a brother in Cavan, and "the life was frightened out of her" when she was asked for £25 as duty on it.

label: text
text: Shanghai, September 8.—Ex-Commander Tong of the Southern Forces, interviewed by the captain of the Japanese warship "Saga," is said to have intimated that the Southern expedition to the north is for the purpose of eushibg Wu Pei-fu and, at the same time, of ousting British influence from the Yangtse-Klang. Tong admits that there are a large number of Russians in the Southern Army.

label: text
text: "Moscow, August 5.—Kuibych", Vice-President of the Council of People's Commissar' is appointed President of the Supreme Council of National Economy and at the same time relieved of his post as head of the Peasant and Workers' Inspection Commissarint. Kuibych's new post was formerly held by Dzérjinsky, the notorious head of the Cheka the greatest organization of execution the world has ever known. Dzérjinsky died recently at Moscow.

label: text
text: Moscow, September 8.—The Pepsidium of the Federal Metal Workers' Union has transferred 10,000 roubles to Shanghai in aid of the workers on strike there.

label: text
text: Peking, September 7.—H. R. H. Prince George, now in this city, expects to visit the Nankow battlefields to-day accompanied by Gen. Chang Hsueh-liang, son of Marshal Chang, who will return to Mukden after returning from the trip to Nankow. The Prince returned here this morning from an extended tour through Kalgan and Tayuan, Shansi province, where he called upon General Yen Hsi-shan.

label: text
text: A census taken by the Japanese police authorities in Peking shows that at the end of last month, there were 1,613 Japanese inhabitants for Peking, including 837 males and 776 females.

label: text
text: Paris, September 11.—The ministerial Council at a plenary session to-day decreed reductions in the French army and that gradually the properties be transferred from military to government control. Some 2,700 permanent officers are to be dismissed. The Council also decreed that 1,200 officers of temporary rank should be eliminated.

label: text
text: Osaka, September 11.—More than 200 earthquakes have been recorded every year since 1923 at Wakayama, 40 miles south of Osaka. The seismologists say that there is no danger of a big earthquake as long as the small ones continue, but the Osaka "Mainichi Shimbun" announces that in order to make a closer observation, the paper is donating a new set of seismological instruments to the Wakayama Observatory.

label: text
text: London, August 29.—Nuremberg.—The organisers of the Nationalist demonstration telegraphed to President Hindeburg, whom they joyfully acclaimed as the leader of the greatest battles in the world's history. General Ludendorf was a notable absentee. He was not invited to participate in the demonstration owing to his breach with Prince Rupprecht and the Envarian Officer's Corps whereby he has been subjected to a social boycott.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL NEWS.

label: text
text: Berlin, August 3.—The former Chancellor, Herr Wirth publishes an article in the "Berliner Taggeplatt," inviting the Republicans to oppose, all manifestations with reactionary tendencies. He affirms that the Austro-German fusion will be for the work of future generations, and insists on the necessity of a complete elucidation of the political atmosphere between Germany, France and Italy.

label: text
text: The Japanese Army, in order to be fully prepared for an emergency, has secured the enactment of a new law providing for the National Mobilisation Preparatory Bureau, in which, however, the army authorities have not counted the labourers as a part of the force, despite the fact that they are an important factor. The mobilisation work after which the army authorities are endeavouring present is chiefly aimed towards mobilising industrial activities in the Empire in time of war. The Miyako.")

label: text
text: On Saturday and Sunday (48 hours) only one case of notifiable disease was reported, this being a Chinese case of enteric fever (typhoid) from the city district.

label: text
text: Mr. F. C. Jenkin sailed for England in the s.s. "Malwa" on Saturday.

label: text
text: Yesterday was the anniversary of the date of the opening and dedication of the Union Church. Kowloon. The anniversary serves, however, are being held next Sunday.

label: text
text: Mr. J. Nienhuys, one of the founders of tobacco-growing in Deli, Sumatra, recently celebrated his ninetieth birthday. This pioneer of one of the most flourishing cultures in the Dutch East Indies, started for the D.E.I. at the age of twenty-three. Native labour was proved a disappointment, and success only came when he recruited Chinese in Penang. In 1869, the Deli Co. was founded. Mr. Nienhuys personally directed affairs in Deli until 1871, when he returned to Holland. He is still, however, a Director of the Deli Co.

label: text
text:
Cairo, September 1.—A wife of the ex-Sultan of Turkey, Shemed Vahieddin, deposed in 1922; who came to Egypt when the Sultan left Turkey, jumped into the Nile to end the misery of destitution. She was rescued, and recently was given shelter in a charitable institution. She has not received a pension from Angora for the last three months.
The Rev. Hugh John Embling has been nominated "Assistant Bishop of the Diocese of Korea.

label: text
text: The King has won the Bakewell Challenge-Cup for the host-Shife colt at Bakewell, Derbyshire, Farmers' Club Show.

label: text
text: Dr. Self, the German Ambassador, left Tokyo for home on the 9th instant. En route the Envoy is to call at Kobe, and then leave for Berlin by the Siberian Line.

label: text
text: Mr. and Mrs. G. D. Waters and their son, well known' residents of Kobe and Shioya, returned to Kobe by the "Empress of Russia" after a vacation in Europe. Mr. Waters is a director of Messrs. Brunner, Mond & Co. (Japan), Ltd.

label: text
text: Peking, September 10.—The British members of the Peking Club entertained at luncheon to-day His Royal Highness Prince George, who is visiting Peking unofficially. Sir Ronald Macleay presided. The function was informal, and there were no speeches.

label: text
text: Peking, September 9.—Admiral Tsai Ting-kan, Minister of Foreign Affairs, gave a dinner in honor of Prince George at nine o'clock last night. Among those present were Sir Ronald Macleay, British Minister in Peking, General Chang Hsueh-liang, Dr. Wellington Koo, Dr. Wang Chung-hui and Mr. Chang Chih-tan.

label: text
text: The men have taken off their red arn hands and wear tri-colour kerchiefs around their necks. Liu himself, who sold out to the Reds and betrayed Wu Pei-fu, is by no means sure of his personal safety, so he has taken a house in the French Concession from which he discharges his duties as Civil Governor and Peace Commissioner of Hankow.

label: text
text: Music lovers will be pleased to hear that a special programme of gramophone music will be presented during “morning coffee” hour at the restaurant of Messrs. Lane, Crawford, Ltd., to-morrow. Starting at 10:45 a.m. the new Orthophonic Victrola will render selections. Messrs. S. Moutrie & Co., Ltd. who are in charge, promise excellent entertainment.

label: text
text: The death is recorded of Mrs. Mary Louise Maire, a grand-daughter of Wordsworth and the only daughter of the poet's son William, at Hydal, Westmortland, aged 76.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” regrets to learn that Mr. A. W. Hill of the Supreme Court has been in the Government Civil Hospital for several weeks suffering from heart trouble and is in a very weak state.

label: text
text: A film produced under Government auspices to show the work of the Conservative Party will be used for political propaganda through out Great Britain and will be set on tour in a special van.

label: text
text: Nanking, September 12.—Mr. MacMurray, American Minister to Peking, on his way to Manila, has arrived here by the Tientsin-Pukow Railway to-day and interviewed General Sun Chuan-fang. Marshal Sun postponed his departure for Kiukiang one or two days, owing to the American Minister's arrival.

label: text
text: Chicago, August 9th—The chewing of gum makes the modern girl's face as hard "as the crockery of a railway luncheon counter," said Mrs. Ruth J. Maurer, speaking at a school of cosmetics. "Human beings were not meant to be ruminating animals, and when they try it there is some kind of a rebellion of nature and the muscles of the jaw become unduly enlarged."

label: text
text: London, September 2.—Speaking at a luncheon given by the New Health Society, its Secretary, Mr. Meredith Atkinson, said that Sir Arbuthnot Lane had not resigned from the British Medical Association on any question connected with the Society, which no longer held any difference with the Association as regards doctors writing to the Press.

label: text
text: The death occurred on August 9th Mr. Edgar Augustus Haddock, principal of Leeds College of Music, aged 68. His father in 1869 bought for £450 a rare Stradivarius dated 2703, which his son Edgar a few years ago sold to Kubelik, the famous violinist, for, it was stated, £210,000. Mr. Haddock, who made his debut at the Crystal Palace in 1883, founded the Leeds College of Music in 1894.
